related_questions.question: What are the new rules for traveling?

text_blocks.snippet: Several new travel rules are taking effect in 2025. Most notably, the REAL ID Act will require a REAL ID-compliant driver's license or other TSA-approved ID for domestic air travel starting May 7, 2025. Additionally, the UK will require a Electronic Travel Authorization (ETA) for US citizens beginning January 8, 2025. Finally, the EU's Entry/Exit System (EES) is expected to become operational in October 2025, impacting how non-EU nationals enter the Schengen Area.
snippet_highlighted_words: the REAL ID Act will require a REAL ID-compliant driver's license or other TSA-approved ID for domestic air travel starting May 7, 2025

list.snippet: Starting May 7, 2025, you will need a REAL ID-compliant driver's license or other acceptable form of identification (like a passport or passport card) to board domestic flights and access certain federal facilities.
You can check if your current state-issued ID is REAL ID compliant by visiting your state's DMV website.
Acceptable forms of ID include: REAL ID-compliant driver's licenses or state-issued photo IDs, enhanced driver's licenses, U.S. passports, U.S. passport cards, and certain DHS trusted traveler cards.
U.S. citizens traveling to the UK will need to apply for an ETA before their trip, starting January 8, 2025.
The ETA is an electronic travel authorization that will cost around $13 and be valid for multiple trips over two years or until your passport expires.
You can apply for the ETA on the official UK ETA website.
The EES will register all non-EU nationals entering the Schengen Area, replacing the manual stamping of passports with electronic recordings.
It will collect passport details and biometric information (fingerprints and facial image).
The EES is expected to become operational in October 2025 and will be phased in over six months.
This system will apply to U.S. citizens traveling to the Schengen Area.

related_questions.question: What countries have US travel advisories?

text_blocks.snippet: The US Department of State issues travel advisories to advise citizens about safety and security conditions in foreign countries. Some countries with current travel advisories include Afghanistan, Central African Republic, Haiti, Lebanon, Sudan, and Venezuela. These advisories range in levels from 1 to 4, with Level 4 indicating "Do Not Travel" due to significant safety risks.
snippet_highlighted_words: Afghanistan, Central African Republic, Haiti, Lebanon, Sudan, and Venezuela

text_blocks.snippet: Here's a more detailed look at some countries with travel advisories:

list.title: Afghanistan:
list.snippet: The US State Department advises against all travel to Afghanistan due to the extremely unstable security situation and critical threat to US citizens.

list.title: Central African Republic:
list.snippet: The State Department advises against travel due to crime, kidnapping, and armed conflict.

list.title: Haiti:
list.snippet: Travel to Haiti is discouraged due to widespread violence, crime, and limited infrastructure.

list.title: Lebanon:
list.snippet: The advisory recommends against travel due to the presence of Hezbollah and the potential for terrorism.

list.title: Sudan:
list.snippet: The State Department advises against travel due to ongoing armed conflict, crime, and kidnapping.

list.title: Venezuela:
list.snippet: The State Department advises against all travel to Venezuela, citing risks including wrongful detention, torture, terrorism, kidnapping, crime, and civil unrest.

text_blocks.snippet: Other countries with travel advisories include:

list.title: North Korea:
list.snippet: US citizens are advised not to travel due to high risk of arrest and long-term detention.

list.title: Iran:
list.snippet: The US government advises against travel to Iran due to the risk of arbitrary arrest and detention.

list.title: Libya:
list.snippet: Travel to Libya is strongly discouraged due to ongoing armed conflict, terrorism, and civil unrest.

list.title: Myanmar:
list.snippet: The State Department advises against travel due to the volatile security situation, including armed conflict and violence.

text_blocks.snippet: Note: The specific reasons for advisories can vary, including armed conflict, terrorism, crime, civil unrest, and health hazards. The US Department of State provides a comprehensive list of travel advisories.
